chunks: Talaq al-ʿiddah is that when a man intends to divorce his wife, he divorces her in a state of purity in which there has been no intercourse, with two just witnesses. Then he takes her back that same day or later before she menstruates, and he has witnesses to her return, until she menstruates. When she becomes pure from that menstruation, he divorces her again, a second divorce, without intercourse, and has witnesses to that. Then he may take her back whenever he wishes before she menstruates, and he has witnesses to her return, and has intercourse with her, and she remains with him until she menstruates a second time. When she becomes pure from that menstruation, he divorces her a third time while she is pure and without intercourse, and has witnesses to that. If he does that, she has become separated from him and is not halal for him until she marries another husband. The minimum form of taking back is that he kisses her or denies the divorce, so his denial of the divorce counts as taking her back. Taking back is permissible without witnesses just as marriage is permissible, but taking back without witnesses is only disliked because of matters of hudud, inheritances, and the ruler.

Whoever divorces his wife for the waiting period three times, one after another as described, and then the woman marries another husband, but he does not consummate with her and then divorces her or dies before consummation, and the woman completes her waiting period, it is not permissible for her first husband to marry her until another man marries her, consummates with her, and tastes her sweetness, then divorces her or dies from her, and she completes her waiting period from him. Then if the first wishes to marry her, he may do so. If a man marries her in mutʿah and consummates with her, then separates from her or dies from her, it is not permissible for her first husband to marry her until another man marries her in a definitive permanent marriage and consummates with her, so that she has entered into the like of what she exited from; then he divorces her or dies from her, and she completes her waiting period from him. Then if the first wishes to marry her, he may do so. If a slave marries her, then he is one of the husbands.

Everyone who divorces his wife for the waiting period, then she marries another husband, then he marries her again, then divorces her for the waiting period, then she marries another husband, then he marries her again, then divorces her for the waiting period, she has become separated from him and is not halal for him after nine divorces, ever.

key_terms.الْمُرَاجَعَةِ: Revocation or taking back the wife during the revocable waiting period.
key_terms.بِشَاهِدَيْنِ عَدْلَيْنِ: In the presence of two just witnesses, a condition mentioned for the divorce.
key_terms.تَزْوِيجًا بَتَاتًا: A definitive permanent marriage, required here as the intervening marriage.
key_terms.تِسْعِ تَطْلِيقَاتٍ: Nine divorces, after which she becomes permanently forbidden to him.
key_terms.جِمَاعٍ: Marital intercourse, which must not have occurred in that period of purity before the divorce.
key_terms.طَلَاقُ الْعِدَّةِ: Divorce carried out in the legally prescribed sequence tied to the waiting period.
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: A state of ritual purity between menstruations in which divorce is to be issued here.
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Temporary marriage, which here does not suffice to make the woman halal again for the first husband.

ai.seo_question: What is ṭalāq al-ʿiddah, and when does a divorced wife become permanently forbidden to her former husband?
ai.summary: This text sets out the fiqh of ṭalāq al-ʿiddah, including the required sequence of divorces, revocation, witnessing, and the conditions under which a woman becomes forbidden to her former husband. It also clarifies when remarriage becomes permissible after an intervening marriage and states the ruling of permanent prohibition after nine such divorces.
